rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı canvasses derivations from sejn, prison, and secc, clay or smearing; he says the latter is possible but unattested as a lexical noun or adjective.
rows.anchor: Zâhirine nazaran “secn” veya “secc” maddelerinden olması muhtemildir

rows.speaker: Ebû Hayyan
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says most derive siccīn as an intensive form from sejn; it may also mean an imprisoning place, though the context favors a book.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hayyan Bahr’da şöyle hulâsa etmiştir

rows.speaker: İkrime
rows.claim: Ikrima glosses siccīn as ruin and abasement, comparing it to reaching the utmost cold.
rows.anchor: İkrime demiştir ki ‘siccîn, hasar ve hevandan ibarettir

rows.speaker: Bazı lügaviyyûn
rows.claim: Some lexicographers say the n in siccīn replaces an l, deriving it from siccīl; if original, it points to sejn.
rows.anchor: Bazı lügaviyyûn da ‘siccînin nûn’u lâm’dan bedeldir

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî
rows.claim: Zamakhshari treats Siccīn as a transferred proper name, declinable because definiteness is its only cause of declension, and as a comprehensive ledger of evil deeds.
rows.anchor: Zemahşerî, hâtim gibi vasıftan menkul ism-i alem olduğunu

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî
rows.claim: The ledger records the deeds of devils, disbelievers, and sinners in clear or marked writing that shows any viewer there is no good in it.
rows.anchor: Siccîn câmi‘bir kitabdır, o, dîvân-ı şerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Siccīn can mean a prison, jailer, or prisoner; Zamakhshari connects the name with confinement and pressure or a dark place beneath the seventh earth where Iblis and his progeny dwell.
rows.anchor: Ona habs u tazyik demek olan ‘secin’den fi‘‘îl olarak ‘siccîn’ tesmiye edilmiştir

rows.speaker: Şeyh Abduh
rows.claim: Abduh proposes that Siccīn contrasts with the upward sense of Illiyyūn and may derive from Abyssinian sençūn, mud, perhaps borrowed into Yemeni usage; the sinners' record is imagined in mud or written with foul ink.
rows.anchor: illiyyûnda te‘allî mânası bulunduğu gibi bunda da teseffül mânası vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı calls Abduh's proposal far-fetched: he documents no Yemeni usage, the proposed words are not close, and a foreign proper name would not be declinable.
rows.anchor: Lâkin Abduh Yemen’de öyle bir isti‘mal bulunduğunu nakl u tesbit etmemiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An Arabic derivation from secc would be closer than Abduh's conjecture, but transmitted explanations favor deriving Siccīn from sejn.
rows.anchor: Çünkü o tasavvur ettiği mâna Arabî olan “secc” maddesinden çıkardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most suitable contextual sense is a prison register or register of a prison, possibly kept by a severe jailer, as the container of the wicked's record.
rows.anchor: füccârın yazısına zarf yapılmasına en yakışan mâna da bir zindan sicili veya sicil zindanı olmasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-mā adrāka stresses that ordinary reasoning cannot determine Siccīn; Elmalılı takes kitābun marqūm as the answer explaining it.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ın üslûbunda mâzî sîgasıyla “vemâ edrâke” denildiği zaman cevâbı bildirilegelmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects treating kitābun marqūm as an appositional replacement, since that would repeat rather than answer the question.
rows.anchor: Onun için bunun bedel değil, “o bir kitâb-ı merkumdur” diye suâle cevap olarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marqūm derives from writing or marking and has five readings: clear sound writing, a mark of the sentence to Hell, a merchant's tag, a sealed or titled record, and an indelible patterned inscription.
rows.anchor: Burada beş mâna verilmiştir; birincisi: Beyyinü’lkitâbe

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings converge on a legible, tamper-proof record delivered plainly and carried out without error.
rows.anchor: Şek ve şüpheden âzâde, tahrif ve tasnî‘den sâlim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud 11:82–83 offers a parallel image of marked stones arranged according to their assigned place of execution.
rows.anchor: سِجِّيلٍۢ مَّنضُودٍۢ مُّسَوَّمَةً عِندَ رَبِّكَ

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir transmits a Prophetic report from Abu Hurayra: Falak is a covered pit in Hell, whereas Siccīn is open.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hüreyre radıyallahu anh’tan; Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem buyurdu ki

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir prefers al-Barāʾ's report that Siccīn is the lowest earth, since Hell is also said to be in the lowest earth.
rows.anchor: İbn Cerîr Berâ hadîsini tercih ederek “siccîn”in arz-ı süflâ ile tefsirini ihtiyar eylemiştir

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب
rows.claim: Al-Barāʾ reports that a wicked soul is rejected at heaven's gate and its record is ordered written in the lowest earth, in Siccīn; the Prophet cites Aʿraf 7:40.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem fâcirin nefsinin semâya çıkarılmasını anlatarak buyurdu ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı clarifies that the report says the record is written in the lowest earth, not that Siccīn itself is the lowest earth; that earth is its location.
rows.anchor: “arz-ı süflâdadır” denilmiş. Şu hâlde arz-ı süflâ “kitâb-ı merkūm”

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The Kashshaf's description of Siccīn as cast beneath the seventh earth likewise treats it as a location there.
rows.anchor: Sâhib-Keşşâf da, “arz-ı sâbi‘ada matruh” demekle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reports place Iblis's boundary in the lowest part of the lowest earth, where the records and souls of the wicked are.
rows.anchor: Bazı rivayetlerde de arz-ı süflânın esfeli İblis’in haddi olduğu haber verilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers deny the Qur'an and the afterlife, while God knows what they conceal within themselves.
rows.anchor: Hatta küfredenler tekzib bile ediyorlar Kur’ân’a ve âhirete yalan diyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yūʿūn comes from wiʿāʾ, vessel, in the causative form; its past form occurs in 70:18, where people gather and store things.
rows.anchor: “Yû‘ûn”, kap mânasına “vi‘â”dan if‘âldir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the concealed motives, corrupt beliefs, and bad aims behind their denial, what they seek to gain, and what they do to believers and enter in their books.
rows.anchor: gönüllerinde ne gibi muzmer fikirler, bozuk akideler, fena maksadlar besliyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to announce painful punishment is ironic: the disbelievers may rejoice at the supposed glad tidings.
rows.anchor: kâfirleri elîm bir azâb ile müjdele de onunla sevinsinler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is generally disconnected when believers are excepted from disbelievers, but connected with respect to believers who had been among the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: istisnâ-yı munkatı‘olursa da kâfirler içinden iman edenlere nazaran muttasıldır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For those who believe and do good, an ungrudged reward means either a reward without indebtedness because earned, or an eternal reward that never ceases.
rows.anchor: mennolunmaz, yani kendi kesbleri olmak itibariyle minnetsiz, yahut kesilmez ebedî

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath concerns forces that charge through a gathered company, penetrate an enemy army, or surround and rout it.
rows.anchor: Bir düşman derneğini, ordusunu tam ortasından vurup içine dalarak yahut çevirip ortaya alarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings, or some members of the species, are deeply ungrateful to their Lord and fail to acknowledge or thank Him for blessings.
rows.anchor: Üzerindeki nimetinin hakkını tanımaz, şükrünü edâ etmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ungrateful person overlooks blessings, remembers hardships, and complains instead of doing his duty to God.
rows.anchor: hep mâruz olduğu mesâib ve müşkilâtı anarak şikâyet ve itiraz eder durur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kanūd is an emphatic form of kefūr, meaning intensely ungrateful; it can also mean one who persistently blames and denies blessings.
rows.anchor: “Kenûd” “anûd” vezninde kefûr, yani çok küfrân-ı nimet edici demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word can describe barren land, an ungrateful wife, a miser who eats alone, someone withholding a due gift, a stingy sinner, or a harsh master who beats servants.
rows.anchor: Bir şey bitirmeyen verimsiz araziye ve kocasının hukūkuna iyiliklerine küfran eden nankör karıya

rows.speaker: çokları
rows.claim: Most commentators take kanūd broadly of human nature as intense ingratitude for blessings.
rows.anchor: Burada ekseriyetle tabî‘at-ı insâniyeye ait olmak üzere çokları

rows.speaker: Zeccâc
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj glosses kanūd as disbeliever; the excerpt marks the citation with an editorial footnote.
rows.anchor: Zeccâc kâfir[^3] demiş, Hasan-ı Basrî

rows.speaker: Hasan-ı Basrî
rows.claim: Hasan al-Basri describes someone who recounts calamities, forgets blessings, and continually reproaches.
rows.anchor: Hasan-ı Basrî mesâibi sayar, nimeti unutur levvâm demiş

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir transmits a Prophetic gloss from Abu Umama: the intensely ungrateful person eats alone, beats his servant, and withholds assistance.
rows.anchor: İbn Cerîr Ebû Ümâme radıyallâhu anh’tan şöyle bir hadis de rivayet eylemiştir

rows.speaker: Taberî
rows.claim: Tabari and others refer the witness pronoun to the Lord: God sees the person's ingratitude, as a warning against sin.
rows.anchor: Taberî gibi bazıları “Rabb”e ircâ‘ederek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı prefers referring the pronoun to the human because the passage centers on him and the next pronoun also refers to him, giving better coherence.
rows.anchor: kelâmın mevzû‘u insan olmak ve bundan sonraki zamir de ona râci‘bulunmak hasebiyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human himself witnesses his ingratitude: his treatment of dependents makes it evident to reflection and conscience; if he does not admit it now, he will testify against himself in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: İnsan öyle olduğuna kendisi şehadet eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says the waw is conjunctive and this clause is a second answer to the oath.
rows.anchor: bu da kasemin ikinci cevâbı demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-khayr often means wealth, as in 2:180; wealth is called good because people want its worldly benefit and imagine it wholly good, a presumption condemned here.
rows.anchor: “Hayr” Kur’ân’ın إِن تَرَكَ خَيْرًا [el-Bakara 2/180] gibi birçok âyetlerinde mal mânasına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of shadīd is miserly: the person loves wealth but refuses to spend it on God's due or public benefit.
rows.anchor: Yani mal ve serveti mutlaka hayır zannederek sevdiği için bahîldir, sıkıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation makes him strong in acquiring and hoarding wealth but weak in paying its due and thanking God.
rows.anchor: Onu kazanmak, eline geçirip toplamak hususunda kavîdir, harîstir

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The Kashshaf offers a reading Elmalılı calls clearer: the person is constricted and displeased by good works requiring money or bodily effort.
rows.anchor: Keşşâf üçüncü bir vecih daha söylemiştir ki daha açık görünür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afalā yaʿlam is a warning that the person will learn the consequences when graves are overturned, as also stated in Infitar 82:4.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i İnfitar’da وَإِذَا ٱلْقُبُورُ بُعْثِرَتْ [82/4] âyetine bak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When what is in the chests is gathered and brought to completion, every hidden secret, intention, and motive will be exposed fully.
rows.anchor: yani gönüllerde saklanan bütün gizli sırlar, niyetler, garazlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ungrateful will then understand their deeds because their Lord knows every atom, inward and outward, past and future, and will make them recognize it.
rows.anchor: Hiçbir zerresinden gāfil değil, içlerini dışlarını hepsini bilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God keeps account even when people forget their deeds, echoing Mujadila 58:6.
rows.anchor: أَحْصَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُ وَنَسُوهُ’dur [el- Mücâdele 58/6]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hoarded wealth whose due was withheld will be heated in Hell to brand foreheads, sides, and backs, as in Tawba 9:35.
rows.anchor: يَوْمَ يُحْمَىٰ عَلَيْهَا فِى نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ فَتُكْوَىٰ بِهَا جِبَاهُهُمْ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening oath gives a worldly example of communities devastated by fiery military attacks.
rows.anchor: ateşler çakarak gelip cemiyetleri perişan eden harb akınları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage urges willingly spending wealth for good works and preparing available force for God's cause, rather than hoarding; it invokes Anfal 8:60.
rows.anchor: Allah yolunda kuvvet hazırlamak için seve seve mal sarfederek hayra çalışmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One may escape death in worldly conquest, but not the eternal punishment when graves are opened and every deed is judged; this calls people to generosity for God.
rows.anchor: ebedî azabdan kurtulmak kābil olmayacağı anlatılarak insanlar Allah için hayırperverliğe sevkolunmuştur

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi says people prepare for burial and worldly gain, though graves, coffins, and shrouds become food for worms; he asks where they prepare for the Merciful Lord.
rows.anchor: Râzî der ki: “Burada vaaz hissesi şudur: Ey insan

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi compares preparing clothes for a child in the womb to God's question whether people prepare for the emergence of all things within the earth.
rows.anchor: Bir kadın bile hâmil olduğu vakit çocuğuna giyecek hazırlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qariʿa follows by describing the outcome before the all-knowing Lord as the dead rise and inner contents are exposed.
rows.anchor: bunu ber vech-i âtî Sûre-i Kāri‘a tâkip edecektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı keeps humaza untranslated because it is also the surah's name.
rows.anchor: Sûrenin de ismi olmak münasebetiyle mealde aynen muhafazasını daha muvâfık gördüğümüz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humaza is an intensive form from hamz that denotes a habitual agent; hamz includes pinching, poking, striking, breaking, squeezing, biting, and throwing down.
rows.anchor: Asıl mefhûmu hemzi çok yapan, âdet edinenler demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In common usage humaza figuratively means a habitual backbiter and slanderer who mocks people and damages their honor, often behind their backs; the physical sense remains available metaphorically.
rows.anchor: örf-i lügatta “hâmiz” ve “hemmâz”dan daha mübalağalı olarak “hümeze”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since metaphor does not exclude literal meaning, the condemnation covers anyone who habitually injures people physically or verbally.
rows.anchor: Kinayeler hakikatin de iradesine mâni‘olmayacağı cihetle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lumaza comes from lemz, spearing criticism or signaling mockery, and denotes a conceited person who habitually finds faults; it can overlap with humaza or differ from it.
rows.anchor: “lemz”den “lümeze” dahi dâima herkesi ta‘yîb etmeyi

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî
rows.claim: Zamakhshari distinguishes humaza as a breaker and lumaza as a critic or stabber; both target people's honor through backbiting, and the form marks habitual conduct.
rows.anchor: Zemahşerî’nin beyânına göre “hümeze”nin aslı kırıcı mânasından

rows.speaker: Ziyâd-ı A‘cem
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir cites Ziyad al-Aʿjam's verse to show that someone feigning affection in person becomes a backbiting, fault-finding person when absent.
rows.anchor: Daha evvel İbn Cerîr de Ziyâd-ı A‘cem’in

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies those against whom God begins with wail as tale-bearers who divide friends and seek people's faults.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan; ‘Allah teâlâ’nın veyl ile başladığı kimseler kimlerdir?’ diye sorulduğunda

rows.speaker: مُجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid's first report assigns humaza to the eater of people's flesh and lumaza to the critic; a second reverses the assignments.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid’den de üç muhtelif kavil rivayet

rows.speaker: مُجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid's third report says one term means eating people's flesh and the other means criticizing, without specifying which is which.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid’den de üç muhtelif kavil rivayet

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Razi reports Ibn Abbas's distinction: humaza is a backbiter and lumaza a fault-finder.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan ‘hümeze’ muğtâb, gıybetçi; ‘lümeze’ ayyâb, ayıpçı

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd distinguishes them by means: humaza is done by hand, lumaza by tongue.
rows.anchor: İbn Zeyd’den: ‘Hümeze’ el ile, ‘lümeze’ lisan ile

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya says humaza occurs to a person's face while lumaza occurs behind the person's back.
rows.anchor: Ebu’l-Âliye’den: ‘Hümeze’ yüze karşı, ‘lümeze’ arkadan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported distinction is open criticism versus covert signaling with the eyebrow and eye.
rows.anchor: ‘Hümeze’ cehren, ‘lümeze’ sırren kaş ve gözle

rows.speaker: رَازِي
rows.claim: A fifth view includes insulting nicknames, as Walid ibn al-Mughira did, and mocking people by imitating their words, actions, or voices.
rows.anchor: Beşincisi: ‘Hümeze lümeze’ nâsa hoşlanmayacakları

rows.speaker: Hasan
rows.claim: Hasan says humaza is winking at a companion to mock him, while lumaza is speaking ill of and faulting one's brothers.
rows.anchor: Altıncısı: Hasan’dan: ‘Hümeze’ gözünü kırparak

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi says the variant glosses return to exposing faults, maliciously or jokingly, on religious or worldly matters, about present or absent people, by words or gestures; all are forbidden, especially against the Prophet, with Hujurat 49:11 cited.
rows.anchor: Bunları naklettikten sonra Râzî şu ihtârı da yapar

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The Kashshaf records a reading with a still mīm describing a silly clown who makes odd, ridiculous chatter and is laughed at and abused.
rows.anchor: Sâhib-Keşşâf bir de demiştir ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatha the forms are active; with sukun they are passive and more degrading, as in duhake/duhke and luʿane/luʿne; all fourteen readings keep the mīms open.
rows.anchor: hatta şâzlar da dâhil olmak üzere on dört kıraatte mîmler üstün okunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah condemns proud slanderers who injure people's dignity while displaying wealth; they are deceived by the previous surah's competition for more, and the following elephant account points to their fate.
rows.anchor: bunlar daha evvelki sûrede geçen tekâsür kendilerini iğfal etmiş olanlardandır

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir transmits from Ibn Abbas that the verse concerns a pagan who mocked and slandered people.
rows.anchor: İbn Cerîr’in Muhammed b. Sa‘d tarîkiyle İbn Abbas’tan tahrîcine göre

rows.speaker: Hasan
rows.claim: Hasan, citing Warqa, says the verse was revealed about Jamil ibn Amir al-Jumahi but is not exclusive to him.
rows.anchor: Hasan, Verkā’dan naklen demiştir ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians say a generic plural can intend one individual, but Elmalılı says the intended meaning is everyone whose traits match the general wording.
rows.anchor: Lâkin diğerlerinin dediği gibi doğrusu maksad hâssı irade değil

rows.speaker: مُجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explicitly says the warning is not restricted to one person.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid de وَيْلٌۭ لِّكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍۢ “bir kimseye has değildir” demiştir

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The Kashshaf reports proposed occasions involving Ahnes ibn Shariq, Umayya ibn Khalaf, and Walid ibn al-Mughira, including Walid's backbiting of the Prophet; a specific cause can still carry a general warning.
rows.anchor: Keşşâf’ta da der ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural pronoun “upon them” at 104:8 supports the general scope of the condemnation.
rows.anchor: diye bunlara cemi‘zamiri gönderilmesi karînedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular relative allathee identifies each member of the class; because it is definite, it cannot modify the indefinite kull, and instead functions as apposition or an accusative of censure.
rows.anchor: Fakat mârife olduğundan nekre olan لِّكُلِّ’ün sıfatı olamaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ruling's focus and the motive behind slander is the person who gathered wealth.
rows.anchor: Gammazlığa, lemmazlığa sâik olan sebep ve illet de bu demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Amir, Hamza, Kisai, Abu Jaʿfar, Rawh, Khalaf, and Aʿmash read jamʿa with a doubled mīm in the intensive form, emphasizing accumulation.
rows.anchor: İbn Âmir, Hamza, Kisâî, Ebû Cafer, Revh, Halef ve A‘meş, mîm’in teşdîdiyle tef‘îl bâbından جَمَعَ okumuşlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person accumulates wealth from everywhere, then keeps counting and increasing it.
rows.anchor: Şuradan buradan bir mal biriktirmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He counts without considering the wealth's sources, obligations, or possible good uses, or he boasts of it before a circle of flatterers and gathers them around himself.
rows.anchor: nereden gelip nereye gitmesi lâzım geleceğini, onunla ne gibi hayırlar yapabileceğini düşünmeyerek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many in the humaza lumaza circle own little themselves but aspire to collect wealth through slander, so they cluster around and count the rich person's wealth.
rows.anchor: Yahut etrafındakilere sade onu saydırıp onunla iftihar etmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative is singular because it can describe each individual, while the later plural pronoun points to the gathered group.
rows.anchor: Sonra da bunların cem‘iyyetine tenbih için عَلَيْهِم diye cemi‘zamiri gönderilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The miser imagines wealth has already made him immortal, trusts it to save him from every danger, and builds all hopes on it.
rows.anchor: Kılacak değil de kılmıştır zanneder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı rejects that presumption: lasting life comes through faith in truth, knowledge, and righteous action, as the preceding surah explained.
rows.anchor: üzere Hakk’a iman ve ilim ile amel-i sâlihtir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in la-yunbadhanna is an oath particle, the nūn emphatic; nabdh means to cast something aside contemptuously.
rows.anchor: Lâm kasem için, “nebz” bir şeyi tahkir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The arrogant slanderer will be thrown into Hutama in utter humiliation.
rows.anchor: kemâl-i hakāret ve sefalet ile atılacaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hutama is a name of Hell alongside Hāwiya, nār ḥāmiya, and jaḥīm; some authorities place it in the fourth, sixth, or second level.
rows.anchor: Hutame”, Kāri‘a’da “hâviye”, “nâr-ı hâmiye”, Tekâsür’de “cahîm” diye ismi geçen cehennemin isimlerindendir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says translating Hutama as old Turkish tamu suits the verse; tamu seems related to dam, prison or dungeon, fitting 17:8's image of Hell as confinement.
rows.anchor: eski Türkçelerde cehenneme “tamu” denildiği cihetle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hutama derives from hatm, to break; the fuʿala pattern conveys habitual action, a relentless crusher.
rows.anchor: vezni de âdet ifade ettiği için “hutame” son derece kırmak âdeti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire consumes whatever it meets; Hutama also names a voracious eater, and the proverb about the worst shepherd calls the herd-destroyer hutama.
rows.anchor: Bir de شَرُّ الرِّعَاءِ اَلْحُطَمَه tâbiri vardır ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hutama matches humaza in form and meaning: one breaks people's dignity, the other breaks and consumes; backbiters eat a brother's flesh per Hujurat 49:12, and fire eats skin and flesh, making the punishment divine justice.
rows.anchor: Sâniyen “hümeze”de başkalarının kadr ü haysiyetini, gönlünü kırmak mânası bulunduğu gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-mā adrāka heightens the horror, asking what kind of terrible Hutama it is.
rows.anchor: Ve bildin mi hutame ne? Yahut ne dehşetli hutame

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling it God's fire conveys majesty and terror; it is beyond comparison with familiar fires, kindled by God's command, and never goes out.
rows.anchor: Allah’a izâfeti lisânımızda da “Allah’ın belâsı” dediğimiz gibi tefhıym ve tehvil içindir

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali marvels that people disobey God while fire boils beneath the earth.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ali kerremallâhu vecheh şöyle demiştir: “Ne acâibdir[^36] o insanlar ki altından ateş kaynayıp dururken

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı invokes contemporary theories that the earth's crust is as thin relative to its inner fire as a membrane over an egg.
rows.anchor: Arz’ın içindeki ateşe nazaran üzerinde bulunduğumuz kabuğu yumurtanın içine nisbetle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire rises over the fuʾād, the inner center of perception, passes through the body to spirits and inward realities, and burns them; it does not kill, as Taha 20:74 says, because evil beliefs and intentions originate there.
rows.anchor: Tenden geçer rûhlara, maneviyâta muttali‘olur, çatar, sarar, canlar yakar

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Peygamber
rows.claim: Razi transmits a Prophetic report that the fire consumes its people until it reaches their hearts and stops, after which God restores their flesh and bones in another creation; Nisa 4:56 supports renewal of skin.
rows.anchor: Râzî’nin zikrettiği üzere, Hazret-i Peygamber’den rivayet olunmuştur ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ittilaʿ literally means rising over; the image of fire enveloping the hearts also includes the brain and conveys total severity.
rows.anchor: “Ittılâ‘” bir şeyin üzerine çıkmaktır

rows.speaker: آلوسي
rows.claim: Alusi says mystics interpret the fire's reaching the hearts as a sign of the severity of spiritual punishment.
rows.anchor: Erbâb-ı işaret bunda rûhânî azâbın şiddetine işaret olduğunu söylerler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muʾṣada means the fire will be shut over them, with its doors closed.
rows.anchor: üzerlerine bastırılıp kapıları kapanacaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extended columns may modify the fire: long bars brace its doors shut, like closing a heated furnace securely.
rows.anchor: O ateşin kapıları kapanırken tazyikle açılmamak için uzun uzun dikmeler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively they may modify the condemned, depicting them immobilized among long logs or pillars they cannot drag away.
rows.anchor: tomruklar içinde kımıldanamayacakları bir surette azab ve işkencelerini tasvir ve beyan olur

rows.speaker: راغب
rows.claim: Raghib and al-Farra call amad a plural of amud, while Abu Ubayda calls it plural of imad; Elmalılı says supports and columns overlap but are not identical.
rows.anchor: Râgıb ve Ferrâ “amûd”un cem‘i demiş

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda takes amad as the plural of imad, a support or prop that need not be a column.
rows.anchor: Ebû Übeyde “imâd”ın cem‘i demiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Bakr, Hamza, Kisai, and Khalaf read umud with both ʿayn and mīm rounded, an unambiguous plural.
rows.anchor: Ebû Bekr, Hamza, Kisâî, Halef ayn’ın ve mîm’in zammıyla “umud” okumuşlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amud means column and connotes support; it can refer to a tribe or army's leader, a sword's ridge, bodily supports, or a person rigid with grief.
rows.anchor: Bir kavmin kıvâm-ı umûru olan ulusuna “amûd-i kavm” denilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amad may point to the bodies of those surrounded by fire or to the immense bodies of the guardians around them.
rows.anchor: o ateş gönüllerini saranların bedenlerine veya onları ihâta etmiş olan zebanilerin cesametlerine

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the columns as pillars of fire surrounding the condemned.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan bunların onları ihâta eden ateş sütunları demek olduğu da mervîdir

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi transmits a marfuʿ report from Abu Hurayra: after sinful believers leave the Fire, angels seal it with fiery covers and columns, leaving no relief or opening and only sighs and groans.
rows.anchor: Hakîm-i Tirmizî’nin Nevâdiru’l-Usûl’de Ebû Hüreyre’den merfû‘an tahric eylediği bir hadiste de şöyle vârid olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı closes by praying to be saved from the Fire and admitted to Paradise with the righteous.
rows.anchor: اَللّٰهُمَّ اَجِرْنَا مِنَ النَّارِ وَأَدْخِلْنَا الْجَنَّةَ مَعَ الأَْبـْرَارِ
